instructions.name: add_collateral_vault
docs: Add a new collateral vault (admin only)

accounts.name: collateral_mint
docs: The new collateral token mint to add

accounts.name: collateral_vault
docs: The vault token account for this collateral

instructions.name: apply_corporate_action
docs: Record a corporate action (split, reverse split, or any other pure
change of share UNITS) by folding its ratio into the market's cumulative
price adjustment.
**What this does.** Nothing, immediately. It writes two integers and
touches no price, no supply, no collateral, no γ. Every stored value
stays exactly as it was, and every outstanding claim is worth exactly
what it was worth one slot earlier. What changes is the INTERPRETATION
of the NEXT raw oracle print: from the following `update_risk_state` on,
an incoming price is multiplied by `num/den` before it is stored.
**Why that is exactly conserving.** A 2-for-1 split halves the price and
doubles the share count; it creates and destroys no value. So the
adjusted price `P_adj = P_raw · num/den` is CONTINUOUS across the event:
identical immediately before and immediately after. Because `l_nav`,
`K = initial_l_price · initial_s_price` and hence `s_nav` are all
functions of `P_adj` alone, every leg's NAV is unchanged too, and the
transfer between longs and shorts is zero by construction.
That is the precise sense in which this is tractable and a spot
RE-ANCHOR is not. Both look like "move the reference price". But a
re-anchor changes the payoff SHAPE — it moves the vertex of the cosh
bowl, so the pair is worth something different afterwards, and it cannot
be made conserving without either moving value between the legs or
redenominating supply. A split changes only the units the shape is
measured in, which is why undoing it in the unit mapping costs nothing.
**Operationally.** Ex-dates are published weeks ahead, so arm the ratio
before the ex-date open and there is no outage at all. Deliberately NOT
auto-detected: the 25% move guard exists to catch a compromised keeper,
and teaching it to recognise a split would hand that same keeper a way
to relabel a bad price as a corporate action.
**Ordering matters below the guard threshold.** A post-action print is
rejected — and the market safely halts — only when `1 − den/num > 25%`,
i.e. ratios above about 1.333. Anything gentler (4:3, 5:4, a stock
dividend) is INDISTINGUISHABLE from a real price move and will be
absorbed as one if this lands late. There is no on-chain backstop for
that case; arming ahead of the ex-date is the control.
Authority-gated, not keeper-gated: this is a governance act on the
market's definition, not part of the hot price loop.

instructions.name: cancel_redemption
docs: Give back the unpaid part of a request and close it (owner only).
Reads no `Market` and needs no keeper, so it works when the market is
paused, the price is stale or the keeper is down. Returns the escrowed
L and S and all rent to the owner. Returns each escrow's ACTUAL balance
(the unpaid remainder plus any atoms someone sent it), so a donation can
never block the close or strand the request slot.

instructions.name: close_market_admin
docs: Close a market account for migration/cleanup.
Uses unchecked account to handle both old and new struct layouts.
Authority is verified by reading raw bytes at offset [8..40].

accounts.name: market
docs: Authority is verified by reading raw bytes [8..40] in the instruction body.

accounts.name: market_advance
docs: may not exist. Read by `advance_outstanding`.

instructions.name: configure_market_advance
docs: Set a market's advance cap and lender (market.authority). Creates the
`MarketAdvance` PDA on first use. `max_advance_bps = 0` turns advances
off. The lender (the token account advances come from and are repaid
to) may change only while nothing is outstanding.

accounts.name: lender
docs: The token account advances come from and are repaid to.

instructions.name: configure_risk_fees
docs: Configure risk-based fee parameters (admin only)

instructions.name: configure_worst_case_quoting
docs: Configure worst-case quoting parameters (admin only)

instructions.name: configure_yield_ceiling
docs: Configure yield ceiling and enable/disable yield management (admin only).
The ceiling may reach 100%: all idle collateral lent and recalled just in time
(Rafael, 2026-10-12). It used to stop at 90%. The keeper's allocator still keeps
a small working float so routine redemptions never wait for a recall.

instructions.name: create_token_metadata
docs: Create Metaplex token metadata for a market's L or S mint.
Must be called by the market authority.
The market PDA is the mint authority and signs the CPI.

accounts.name: mint
docs: The L or S mint to create metadata for.
Must be either market.long_mint or market.short_mint.

instructions.name: deploy_collateral_to_yield
docs: Deploy a portion of idle collateral to a lending protocol (keeper only).
This instruction moves USDC from the collateral vault to the keeper's
intermediary account. The keeper then deposits it into Kamino/MarginFi
in the next instruction of the same atomic transaction.
AUDIT H2 (custody — REMAINING WORK, needs venue integration + governance):
funds transit a keeper-owned ATA with NO on-chain proof they reach a
venue; `deployed_to_yield` is a keeper-asserted scalar. The bound today is
`yield_ceiling_bps` (a fraction of THIS market's total_collateral). Full
fix (not doable without external CPI wiring / an ops decision):
1. CPI directly into a WHITELISTED venue so the deposit is proven
on-chain (or constrain the destination to an admin-approved
intermediary pubkey — needs a new Market field + realloc migration).
2. Move `configure_yield_ceiling` + this instruction's authority behind
a multisig/timelock (ops).
3. Per-tx / rolling-window cap (needs Market window state → realloc).
Compensating controls now: `mark_yield_impairment` (M2) socializes a
venue loss; the off-chain `yield-vault-reconciler` + `solvency-monitor`
scripts alert when venue-redeemable < deployed_to_yield.

accounts.name: keeper
docs: Must be the market's keeper_authority

accounts.name: collateral_vault
docs: Collateral vault owned by the market PDA

accounts.name: keeper_usdc_account
docs: Keeper's USDC intermediary account (destination before lending deposit).
Must be owned by the keeper signer.

instructions.name: donate_to_vault
docs: Permissionless top-up of the collateral vault.
Increases `total_collateral` and the vault balance without minting any
tokens, so every holder's collateralization strictly improves. It funds
the protocol's safety buffer and nothing else: the donor receives no
reward. (A per-donor fee waiver used to be granted here; it was removed
on 13 Oct 2026, audit MR-13.)

accounts.name: collateral_vault
docs: Per-market collateral vault — must match the one bound to this market
at init. Owned by the Market PDA.

accounts.name: donor_collateral
docs: Source ATA. Holds the cUSDC the donor is sending in. Must hold the
market's collateral mint; the SPL transfer below validates the mint
match implicitly (cross-mint transfers fail in the SPL token program).

instructions.name: enable_multi_collateral
docs: Enable multi-collateral mode for a market (admin only)

instructions.name: fund_collateral
docs: Admin top-up of a market's collateral (listing buffers, redistribution).
Transfers `amount` cUSDC from the authority's token account into
`market.collateral_vault` and credits `total_collateral`. Like
`donate_to_vault` there is no price-freshness gate: a deposit only
raises the ratio.

accounts.name: authority_collateral
docs: The authority's cUSDC. SPL Token enforces that `authority` owns it.

instructions.name: fund_collateral_from
docs: CPI-friendly twin of `fund_collateral`. The market authority still signs
(`has_one = authority`), but the cUSDC comes from `funder_collateral`,
a token account owned by a SEPARATE signer `funder`, which may be a PDA
signing through CPI (the CLP's GlobalClp backstopping a market from its
treasury). Credits `total_collateral` exactly like `fund_collateral` and
emits the same `CollateralFunded` event.

accounts.name: authority
docs: Must equal `market.authority`.

accounts.name: funder
docs: Owner of `funder_collateral`; may be a PDA signing through CPI.

instructions.name: harvest_collateral_yield
docs: Harvest net collateral yield INTO this market's collateral (keeper only).
Call after recall_collateral_from_yield: principal goes back to the vault,
then this deposits the net interest (yield_amount) into the same vault and
credits it to `total_collateral`, so the yield raises this market's CR by
exactly that amount. Collateral yield is protocol-side; whatever ends up
above the buffer target still reaches the CLP through `withdraw_excess_to_clp`.

accounts.name: keeper_usdc_account
docs: Keeper's USDC source account (holds the net yield)

accounts.name: collateral_vault
docs: The market's collateral vault: the yield funds this market's CR. Same slot
as the former `clp_vault`, so the wire layout is unchanged.

instructions.name: initialize_market
docs: Initialize a new synthetic asset market (admin only: the signer must be
this program's upgrade authority).

accounts.name: program
docs: Admin gate: the signer must be this program's upgrade authority, so nobody
else can squat a future symbol's Market PDA and become its `authority`.
Appended LAST so pre-existing account indices stay stable for hand-built
encoders.

instructions.name: keeper_burn_single
docs: Keeper-authorized single-side BURN. Removes one side from the
keeper's wallet WITHOUT paying out collateral from the vault.
Purpose: residual cleanup for arb cycles where a `keeper_mint_single`
produced tokens that didn't fully fill on the DEX. The current
`keeper_redeem_single` path pays the keeper out at *current* NAV,
which (a) drains the vault when NAV has drifted upward since mint
and (b) hides the inventory cost as silent vault drift instead of
an explicit keeper-side P&L line.
Burning the residual instead:
- vault keeps the original mint-time deposit (solvency-safe)
- total_l/s_supply decrements (asymmetry no worse than at mint)
- keeper team eats the cost of unsold inventory (visible in P&L)
Does NOT decrement `total_collateral` — that field tracks cUSDC,
and no cUSDC is leaving the vault. Per-token collateralization
strictly improves: same numerator, smaller denominator (one fewer
token outstanding).

instructions.name: keeper_mint_single
docs: Keeper-authorized single-side mint. Deposits collateral, mints ONLY one
side (L or S). No fees, no worst-case discount, no dev tax — the keeper
is the protocol's own arber and is trusted to:
1. Sign with `market.keeper_authority`
2. Always close any single-side position within the same arb cycle
(mint L_only → sell L → cUSDC) so net inventory is zero between ticks
Uses the base TWAP price (or oracle in Normal). The keeper paying full
NAV for one side preserves overall solvency: collateral_vault grows by
exactly the NAV value of the new tokens. Where paired-mint required
matching supplies (L_supply == S_supply) for invariant convenience, the
per-token NAV-collateralization here gives us the same "claim ≤
collateral" guarantee at every NAV(t) — supplies just drift, which is
fine for transient keeper inventory.

instructions.name: keeper_redeem_single
docs: Keeper-authorized single-side redeem. Burns one side (L or S), returns
collateral at NAV. No fees, no worst-case adjustment.

instructions.name: mark_yield_impairment
docs: Write down an impaired yield deployment (admin/governance only; audit M2).
`recall_collateral_from_yield` only ever decrements `deployed_to_yield` by
what physically returns, and never touches `total_collateral`. So if a
lending venue freezes or loses principal, `total_collateral` (the solvency
source of truth the CR/haircut math reads) keeps reporting phantom
backing: the CR check returns "fully collateralized", early redeemers exit
at par, and stragglers eat 100% of the loss (hidden insolvency).
This instruction realizes the loss by decrementing BOTH `deployed_to_yield`
(the funds are gone from the venue) AND `total_collateral` (real backing
shrank). The pro-rata `solvency_haircut_gross` then measures true CR and
SOCIALIZES the loss uniformly across all remaining holders. Gated on the
admin `authority` (not the keeper): writing down collateral is a governance
action, and this can only REDUCE reported backing (never inflate it), so a
mistaken call is conservative, never a drain.

instructions.name: mint_paired
docs: Mint paired L + S tokens by depositing collateral
This is the ONLY way to create new tokens - always mints both L and S
Invariant: L_value + S_value = collateral_amount (always)
Uses TWAP for pricing in non-Normal risk states for stability

instructions.name: permissionless_burn
docs: Permissionless single-side burn — anyone can call to burn L or S
tokens from their own ATA, reducing `total_l_supply` /
`total_s_supply` accordingly. NO collateral payout.
Used for:
1. Voluntary forfeiture (e.g. admin burning recovered tokens to
reduce supply asymmetry).
2. CLP-program CPI: `clp_burn_excess` calls this with the
CLP-PDA as the source-account owner / signer (via
`invoke_signed` with the CLP PDA seeds), letting the CLP
retire its own L/S inventory after a zombie-pool drain.
SAFETY: this MUST never burn collateral. Accounts struct binds
`long_mint` and `short_mint` to `market.long_mint` /
`market.short_mint`, and the `source_account.mint` is validated
against the appropriate side mint at runtime. The collateral_mint
is never reachable via this code path.

accounts.name: authority
docs: Owner of `source_account`. SPL Token enforces signer == owner on
the burn CPI, so a malicious caller cannot burn someone else's tokens.

accounts.name: source_account
docs: Token account whose tokens are being burned. Must be owned by
`authority` and hold the L or S mint matching `is_long`.

instructions.name: realloc_market
docs: Grow a Market account to the current struct size. MUST be run for every
live market immediately after any deploy that adds fields — until it is,
the account is too short to deserialize and EVERY other instruction on
that market fails.
Validated by hand because the account is deliberately untyped (see
`ReallocMarket`): owner, discriminator, then `authority`, which is the
first field and therefore at a fixed offset that no field addition can
move. Idempotent — an already-grown account is left alone.

accounts.name: market
docs: at a fixed offset). It CANNOT be `Account<'info, Market>`: Anchor
deserializes a typed account inside `try_accounts`, before any `realloc`
constraint runs, so an account that is too SMALL for the current struct
fails to deserialize and can never reach the very instruction that would
grow it. Typing this account is what would make the migration
impossible.

instructions.name: reanchor_gamma
docs: Renew the γ charging budget by folding the accumulated decay into the
short anchor. Zero-arg and authority-gated.
`initial_s_price ← floor(initial_s_price · γ / 1e9)`, then `γ ← 1.0`.
Short NAV is `(initial_l · initial_s / P) · γ`, so moving γ into the
anchor and resetting it leaves every holder's claim IDENTICAL at every
price. Nobody is refunded and nothing is taken — burned budget stays
burned. What changes is that charging can continue: σ² funding never
terminates, so without renewal a persistently volatile market pins at
GAMMA_FLOOR and simply stops charging while the exposure carries on.
After this, the floor is a per-EPOCH fault bound rather than a lifetime
ceiling, which is what it was always meant to be.
Deliberately NOT routed through `set_s_gamma_index`: that path's ratchet
rejects a raise by design, and a two-transaction fold would leave a live
on-chain window where the market is mispriced between the two writes.
The epoch bump is what protects that window here — any decay post
computed against the old epoch fails its CAS instead of re-charging the
whole folded epoch.

instructions.name: rebalance_collateral
docs: Keeper-authorized CROSS-MARKET collateral move (the rebalance EXECUTION): transfer
up to `amount` cUSDC from `from_market`'s collateral vault directly to `to_market`'s —
moving EXCESS from an over-collateralized market to fund an under-collateralized one
FASTER, instead of waiting for fresh capital. The move is CLAMPED to what the source
can spare: collateral above its OWN dynamic target at the stored price (the planner's
"never drain below own CR" constraint, on-chain), capped by its liquid collateral.
The keeper plans at its own price, so a request a hair over that amount moves the
safe amount instead of reverting; only a source with nothing to spare fails. Both
markets must share the keeper authority. NAV = the source's keeper-posted TWAP
(freshness-gated). Mirror amounts come from collateral_rebalancer::plan_rebalance.

accounts.name: to_market
docs: Must differ from `from_market`: both copies are written back on exit and the
destination's (credited) copy lands last, so a self-move would mint ledger.

accounts.name: keeper
docs: Shared keeper authority — must be both markets' keeper_authority.

instructions.name: recall_collateral_from_yield
docs: Recall collateral previously deployed to a lending protocol (keeper only).
The keeper first withdraws from Kamino/MarginFi (returning principal to
keeper's ATA), then calls this instruction in the same transaction to
move the funds back into the collateral vault and update accounting.

accounts.name: collateral_vault
docs: Collateral vault (destination for recalled funds)

accounts.name: keeper_usdc_account
docs: Keeper's USDC account (source — keeper has withdrawn from lending protocol)

instructions.name: receive_advance
docs: Take a liquidity advance into the collateral vault. `market.authority`
signs (`has_one`) and so does the `funder` who owns the lender account,
which is the GlobalClp PDA when the CLP's `advance_to_market` calls
this. The cash is NOT credited to `total_collateral`: CR and the
haircut never see it, and only `settle_redemption` and `repay_advance`
can spend it. Capped at `max_advance_bps` of `total_collateral`.

accounts.name: funder
docs: Owner of the lender account; the GlobalClp PDA signing through CPI.

instructions.name: redeem_paired
docs: Redeem paired L + S tokens to withdraw collateral
User must provide both L and S tokens to redeem
The combined value of L + S = collateral returned
Uses TWAP for pricing in non-Normal risk states for stability
`l_amount` and `s_amount` are the most of each leg to burn: the
redemption burns the largest value-balanced pair inside them at the
worst-case redeem NAVs, and the rest of the larger leg stays in the
wallet (sell it through the trading path). Audit MR-2: a lopsided
paired redeem was an instant one-leg sale at the stored price. The
market's CLP redeeming its own inventory (`vault_redeem_pairs`) burns
exactly what it asks.
A balanced burn moves the market's net exposure by less than $1, so the
exposure accounts of `exposure::check_redemption` (the market's CLP
account, then the pool long and short synth vaults and the CLP's long
and short token accounts) are no longer needed; the check stays as a guard.

instructions.name: redeem_single_for_vault
docs: CLP-authorized single-side redeem from the CLP vault. Mirror of
`keeper_redeem_single` but:
- source ATAs are CLP-PDA-owned (the L/S inventory the keeper holds
for market-making, not the keeper-wallet ATAs);
- destination cUSDC is `clp_vault` (the per-market working-capital
ATA), not the keeper's USDC ATA;
- signer is the CLP PDA (validated by `seeds = [b"clp", market]`
under the canonical CLP program ID), entered via CPI from the
CLP program's `vault_redeem_single` wrapper.
Solvency: identical buffer impact as paired redeem. Each L/S token
claims `L_NAV` / `S_NAV` USDC independently — burning N S tokens
drops total_claims by N×S_NAV and pays out N×S_NAV from
collateral_vault, so `buffer = collateral - total_claims` is
preserved exactly. See the discussion in the rebalancer design doc;
the over-collateralization buffer that exists pre-call still exists
post-call. We additionally floor at CR ≥ 100% (same as
`keeper_redeem_single`) — refuse to make an underwater vault worse.

accounts.name: clp_pda
docs: CLP PDA, signing via CPI with seeds [b"clp", market.key()].
Identity validated in the ix body — the body recomputes
`find_program_address([b"clp", market], <CLP_PROGRAM_ID>)` and
rejects any other key. The `Signer<'info>` type enforces that
the runtime saw a signature.

accounts.name: clp_vault
docs: CLP's USDC ATA — destination for the redemption payout. Owner
must be the CLP PDA (validated by Anchor against `clp_pda.key()`).

accounts.name: clp_long_account
docs: CLP's L-token ATA — burn source when `is_long=true`.

accounts.name: clp_short_account
docs: CLP's S-token ATA — burn source when `is_long=false`.

instructions.name: repay_advance
docs: Repay the advance from the vault to its lender (market.authority or
keeper). Never more than is outstanding, and the vault keeps the
market's own liquid share (`redemption::repay_allowed`), so a repay can
only return the advance's own cash. The keeper calls it when the
market's own recall lands, before that cash is lent again.

accounts.name: signer
docs: market.authority or market.keeper_authority. Safe for the keeper: the
money can only go back to the recorded lender.

instructions.name: request_redemption
docs: Queue a paired redemption the vault cannot pay now. The L and S move
into escrow token accounts owned by the request PDA; the keeper pays
the request (in parts if need be) with `settle_redemption`, and the
owner can `cancel_redemption` the unpaid rest at any time. Same active,
Stress, price-freshness and $10-minimum checks as `redeem_paired`.
Like `redeem_paired`, the amounts are maxima: only the largest
value-balanced pair inside them goes into escrow (audit MR-2), and the
rest stays with the owner. Settles burn the escrow pro rata, so the
request stays balanced. Remaining accounts as for `redeem_paired`.

instructions.name: set_buffer_target
docs: Keeper posts the DYNAMIC overcollateralization buffer (bps over parity) for this
market: the per-market solvency target.
Sized off σ-regime + live inventory (keeper vol_model::dynamic_buffer). Clamped on-chain
to [MIN_BUFFER_BPS, MAX_BUFFER_BPS] so a bad write can't drop the target below the
solvency floor or balloon it absurdly. Called only when the target moves meaningfully
(the buffer drifts slowly), so it's off the hot TWAP path.

instructions.name: set_s_gamma_index
docs: Keeper posts the short-leg volatility-decay scalar γ (1e9 = 1.0). It may
only ever RATCHET DOWN — raising it would retroactively restore short
claims the protocol already banked as surplus, so an increase is
rejected. A genuine reset to 1.0 (a deliberate re-anchor settlement) is
an authority action and intentionally NOT reachable from this keeper path.
Every abnormal write is REJECTED and logged rather than quietly reshaped.
The old code clamped its argument into range, so a single hot-key tx
asking for zero silently became a write to the floor — a −50% mark on
every short, indistinguishable in the logs from an ordinary post. The
bounds are now:
- range: the argument must already be within `[GAMMA_FLOOR, GAMMA_ONE]`,
- ratchet: it may not exceed the current γ,
- per-tx: at most `GAMMA_MAX_STEP_1E9` of decay in one write,
- per-day: at most `GAMMA_MAX_DAY_DECAY_1E9` in any 24h bucket,
- epoch: `expected_epoch` must match, so a post computed before a
re-anchor cannot land after it and re-charge the folded epoch.
Caps bound a fault's blast radius; they cannot catch a slow bleed of
individually-valid posts (which is exactly how OIL burned). Telemetry is
load-bearing for that class — `gamma_last_write_ts` exists so an auditor
can alarm on writer silence too.
Arguments are wrapped in ONE struct deliberately: the v1.45 build
toolchain miscompiles per-argument borsh offsets on multi-arg
instructions (it read a fee from inside a pubkey), and a single struct
is the shape that survives it.

instructions.name: settle_redemption
docs: Pay the largest part of a request the vault's cash covers now (keeper
only), up to `max_l_amount` of L with the matching pro-rata S. Prices,
haircuts and charges fee + dev tax exactly like `redeem_paired`
(`redemption::quote_at_navs`), burns that part from escrow and pays the
owner. Unlike the instant path it may spend the treasury advance's cash
(that is what the advance is for), but never more than the vault holds.
When the request is fully paid and `owner` is passed, the escrows and
the request close and their rent goes back to the owner; without
`owner` an empty request waits for the owner's `cancel_redemption`.

accounts.name: keeper
docs: The keeper. Same signer as `recall_collateral_from_yield`, so a recall
and the settle it pays for share one transaction.

accounts.name: owner_collateral
docs: Where the owner is paid: any cUSDC account the request owner owns.

accounts.name: owner
docs: The request owner, receiving the rent when the last part closes the
request. Optional so the settle still fits beside a large venue recall;
must equal `request.owner` when present.

instructions.name: update_collateral_vault
docs: Update collateral vault configuration (admin only)

instructions.name: update_fee_recipient
docs: Update the fee recipient for a market (admin only).
Set to the CLP vault PDA to route protocol fees to the LP vault.

instructions.name: update_keeper_authority
docs: Update the keeper authority for an existing market (admin only).

instructions.name: update_market
docs: Update market parameters (admin only)

instructions.name: update_market_oracle
docs: Update the oracle account/type for an existing market (admin only).

instructions.name: update_risk_state
docs: Update risk state and TWAP from oracle (keeper only)
This should be called regularly by keepers after updating oracle observations

instructions.name: update_risk_state_v2
docs: Timestamped keeper price. Revalidated at execution so a transaction built
before a split cannot land afterward with a pre-split raw print.

instructions.name: withdraw_excess_to_clp
docs: Withdraw EXCESS collateral from a market's `collateral_vault` to
the per-market CLP vault. Inverse of `donate_to_vault` — used to
rebalance idle equity from over-collateralized markets back to
the CLP, where it can be redeployed as bin-book liquidity, paid
out via `admin_withdraw`, etc.
Admin-gated (signer == market.authority).
SAFETY: enforces a minimum-collateralization floor at withdrawal
time. The post-withdrawal `total_collateral` must remain at or
above `liability_at_NAV × market.target_ratio_bps() / 10_000`, so the
vault stays at or above its own solvency target and the 100% line.
If the live ratio is uncomputable (fresh market, zero supply), no
withdrawal is allowed — there's no liability denominator and no
need to drain anyway.

accounts.name: collateral_vault
docs: Market's collateral vault — source of the drain. Owned by the
Market PDA which signs the SPL transfer via PDA seeds.

accounts.name: clp_vault
docs: CLP vault — destination ATA. Must be the canonical CLP vault for
this market (ATA owned by the CLP PDA derived from the market).
We don't deserialize the CLP account here — just enforce that
the destination's owner is the expected CLP PDA via constraint.

accounts.name: clp_pda
docs: CLP PDA — used as the seed/owner anchor for `clp_vault`. We don't
dereference it (could be uninitialized as far as this ix cares),
but we validate its derivation matches the canonical CLP PDA for
this market via the seeds constraint.

accounts.name: clp_program_id
docs: scope `clp_pda`'s seed derivation.

instructions.name: write_off_advance
docs: Absorb a venue loss into the treasury's advance first (authority only).
The treasury is first-loss capital, so a loss is charged to the
outstanding advance before any holder: `deployed_to_yield` (the lost
principal) and `outstanding` (the treasury's claim) both drop by
`amount`, `total_collateral` is untouched and no cash moves, so slack is
unchanged. A loss beyond the advance goes through `mark_yield_impairment`,
which refuses while anything is still outstanding.

errors.name: MarketNotActive
errors.msg: Market is not active

errors.name: InvalidAmount
errors.msg: Invalid amount

errors.name: InsufficientCollateral

types.name: CollateralFunded
docs: Emitted when the authority tops up a market's collateral.

types.name: CollateralType
docs: Collateral type identifier

types.name: CollateralVault
docs: Individual collateral vault for a specific stablecoin
Each stablecoin has its own vault for blast-radius containment

fields.name: mint
docs: Mint address of this collateral token

fields.name: vault
docs: Vault token account address

fields.name: collateral_type
docs: Type of collateral (for provenance)

fields.name: total_deposited
docs: Total amount deposited in this vault

fields.name: is_active
docs: Whether this vault is active for deposits

fields.name: weight_bps
docs: Weight for collateral (100 = 1:1, 95 = 0.95:1 for riskier stables)

types.name: ConfigureRiskFeesParams
docs: `configure_risk_fees` arguments, in their wire order. One struct, not 5 separate
arguments: the v1.45 SBPF-v2 toolchain garbles narrow arguments passed this
late (configure_swap dropped max_confidence_bps and collateral_floor_bps).
Same bytes on the wire, so existing callers are unaffected.

types.name: CorporateActionApplied
docs: Emitted on every corporate action. The on-chain record of a units change —
the thing an auditor needs to reconcile a synth's price series against the
underlying's unadjusted one.

fields.name: effective_ts
docs: When the new pair becomes live. Equals `ts` for an immediate
application, the ex-date open for an armed one.

fields.name: armed
docs: True if this was armed ahead of its ex-date rather than applied now.

fields.name: price_at_apply
docs: The quoted price at the moment of application, which this instruction
does not modify. Present so the event alone shows the action was
price-neutral.

types.name: CorporateActionParams
docs: Arguments for `apply_corporate_action`, in ONE struct — same reason as
`SetGammaParams`: the v1.45 build toolchain miscompiles per-argument borsh
offsets on multi-arg instructions, and a single struct is the shape that
survives it. Wire format is identical.

fields.name: ratio_num
docs: `new_shares` side of the action ratio. A 2-for-1 split is `num = 2`.

fields.name: ratio_den
docs: `old_shares` side. A 1-for-10 reverse split is `num = 1, den = 10`.

fields.name: effective_ts
docs: Unix ts from which the ratio applies — set it to the ex-date OPEN, the
first instant a venue quotes the post-action price.
`0`, or any value at or before now, applies immediately: the recovery
path when an action was missed and the market has already halted.
A future value ARMS it, leaving pre-ex prints read exactly as they are
today. Arming without this gate is worse than doing nothing — the
adjustment would multiply a still-unsplit price and the 25% move guard
would reject every push from the moment of arming until the ex-date.

types.name: GammaReanchored
docs: Emitted on every re-anchor. Deployment, not first invocation, is the
disclosure trigger — this is the on-chain record of an epoch boundary.

types.name: InitMarketParams
docs: Args for `initialize_market`, passed as a single struct so the borsh
deserialize is ONE unit. The v1.45 SBF toolchain miscompiles the per-arg
field-offset assignment when these are 7 separate scalar args (it reads
`mint_fee_bps` from inside the keeper pubkey). The wire format is byte-for-byte
identical to the old 7-arg form, so off-chain callers are unaffected.

fields.name: collateral_mint
docs: Primary collateral mint (legacy single-collateral mode)

fields.name: collateral_vault
docs: Primary collateral vault (legacy)

fields.name: multi_collateral_enabled
docs: Whether multi-collateral mode is enabled

fields.name: collateral_vault_count
docs: Number of active collateral vaults

fields.name: collateral_vaults
docs: Collateral vaults for multi-stable support

fields.name: initial_l_price
docs: Initial Long token price (used for Short NAV calculation)

fields.name: initial_s_price
docs: Initial Short token price

fields.name: mint_fee_bps
docs: Mint fee in basis points (e.g., 10 = 0.1%)

fields.name: redeem_fee_bps
docs: Redeem fee in basis points

fields.name: total_l_supply
docs: Total supply of Long tokens. Paired mint/redeem keeps this equal to
`total_s_supply`; single-side keeper mint/redeem (`keeper_mint_single`,
see lib.rs) intentionally moves only one side, so the two supplies can
diverge, giving a first-order (directional) delta the γ decay does NOT charge.

fields.name: total_s_supply
docs: Total supply of Short tokens. Equal to `total_l_supply` under paired
mint/redeem, but single-side keeper mint/redeem deliberately lets it
diverge (see `total_l_supply` above).

fields.name: total_collateral
docs: Total collateral locked (sum across all vaults)

fields.name: risk_state
docs: Current risk state (updated by keepers from oracle)

fields.name: risk_state_updated_at
docs: Last time risk state was updated

fields.name: risk_fee_config
docs: Risk-based fee configuration

fields.name: user_twap_price
docs: TWAP price for user quoting (updated by keepers)

fields.name: twap_updated_at
docs: Last TWAP update time

fields.name: worst_case_config
docs: Configuration for worst-case quoting

fields.name: oracle_confidence
docs: Oracle confidence interval (updated by keepers)

fields.name: keeper_authority
docs: Whitelisted keeper authority that is allowed to update risk state

fields.name: dev_tax_pct
docs: Dev tax percentage (updated by keeper based on CLP TVL tiers)

fields.name: yield_ceiling_bps
docs: Maximum fraction of total_collateral deployable to yield protocols (basis points).
Default: 6000 (60%). Remaining 40% stays liquid to cover redemptions.

fields.name: deployed_to_yield
docs: Amount of collateral currently deployed to external lending protocols.
Invariant: deployed_to_yield <= total_collateral * yield_ceiling_bps / 10_000

fields.name: total_yield_harvested
docs: Cumulative yield harvested to CLP vault (never decrements, informational).

fields.name: yield_enabled
docs: Whether collateral yield deployment is enabled for this market.

fields.name: buffer_target_bps
docs: Keeper-posted overcollateralization buffer (bps OVER parity), the dynamic
solvency target. Target ratio = 10_000 + buffer_target_bps, clamped to
[MIN_BUFFER_BPS, MAX_BUFFER_BPS]. 0 (legacy/unset) is treated as the default
200 (102%) by `target_ratio_bps()`, so old accounts behave as before until the
keeper posts a value. Sized from σ-regime + live inventory (vol_model::dynamic_buffer).

fields.name: s_gamma_index
docs: Keeper-posted decay scalar on the SHORT NAV, in 1e9 fixed point
(1_000_000_000 = 1.0 = no decay). The effective short NAV is
`(K / l_nav) · s_gamma_index / 1e9`. It only ever ratchets DOWN, by the
realized variance the short pair accrues, so holding the short across a
choppy path costs the decay, which banks as collateral surplus (the
long leg is never touched). `0` (legacy/unset) is read as 1e9 by
`short_gamma_index()`, so old accounts behave exactly as before until
the keeper posts a value. NOT a perp funding rate; there is no periodic
cash transfer; it is a structural mark on the short token's value, so the
1:1 paired round-trip and buy-and-hold mechanics are unchanged at a fixed γ.

fields.name: gamma_day_start_ts
docs: Unix ts the current γ day-bucket opened. 0 = no bucket yet.

fields.name: gamma_day_decay_1e9
docs: γ index units (1e9) decayed inside the current day-bucket. TELEMETRY
ONLY: tracked so an auditor can see the day's total, never enforced.

fields.name: gamma_last_write_ts
docs: Unix ts of the last accepted γ write. Lets an auditor alarm on writer
SILENCE, the failure mode no cap can catch, because it looks like calm.

fields.name: gamma_epoch
docs: Bumped by a re-anchor. Carried in `SetGammaParams` as a CAS so a decay
post computed against a pre-re-anchor γ can never land after the fold
and re-charge the whole epoch.

fields.name: reanchor_count
docs: How many re-anchors this market has seen. 0 = never.

fields.name: genesis_s_price
docs: `initial_s_price` as of genesis, before any re-anchor folded γ into it.
Backfilled lazily on the first re-anchor; 0 = never re-anchored, so the
live `initial_s_price` IS the genesis value.

fields.name: last_reanchor_ts
docs: Unix ts of the last re-anchor. 0 = never.

fields.name: short_payoff_cap_c_1e9
docs: Reserved for the capped short payoff `S = γ·min(K/P, C·K/P₀)` (1e9
fixed). The instruction ships in upgrade #2; the FIELD lands here so
that upgrade is instructions-only and needs no second realloc.
0 = unset = uncapped, i.e. exactly today's behavior.

fields.name: price_adjust_den
docs: Denominator of the cumulative corporate-action ratio. See
`price_adjust_num`. 0 = unset = identity.

fields.name: price_adjust_pending_num
docs: A corporate action ARMED AHEAD of its ex-date: the cumulative pair that
becomes live at `price_adjust_effective_ts`. Until then the current
`price_adjust_num/den` keeps applying.
This exists because arming a ratio early is otherwise actively harmful,
not merely useless. The adjustment multiplies the NEXT raw print, and
before the ex-date that print is still PRE-split, so an early 2:1 would
double the stored price, the 25% move guard would reject every push, and
the market would halt from the moment of arming until the split actually
happened. Gating on a timestamp is what makes "schedule it weeks ahead"
a true statement instead of a longer outage.

fields.name: price_adjust_pending_den
docs: Denominator of the pending pair. See `price_adjust_pending_num`.

fields.name: price_adjust_effective_ts
docs: Unix ts from which the pending pair applies. 0 = nothing pending.
Set it to the ex-date OPEN, the first instant a venue quotes the
post-action price. Misalignment is bounded and self-correcting for
ratios above ~1.333: a print on the wrong side of the boundary is
REJECTED by the 25% guard, not absorbed, so an early or late `ts` costs
rejected pushes rather than a mispriced book. Below ~1.333 nothing
rejects it and the alignment is the only control.

fields.name: price_adjust_last_effective_ts
docs: Most recent activated units boundary, retained after promotion and rescheduling.

types.name: MarketAdvance
docs: The treasury's reversible liquidity advance to one market (r58 lever 3).
PDA seeds: `[b"market_advance", market]`. The advance's cash sits in the
market's collateral vault but is NOT `total_collateral`: CR and the haircut
never count it, and every pre-existing outflow is gated on the market's own
liquid share, so only `settle_redemption` and `repay_advance` spend it.
Invariant: `vault + deployed_to_yield = total_collateral + outstanding + slack`.

fields.name: lender
docs: The only token account an advance may come from and be repaid to
(the CLP global vault). Changeable only while nothing is outstanding.

fields.name: max_advance_bps
docs: Cap: `outstanding ≤ max_advance_bps × total_collateral / 10_000`.
0 = advances off. r58's 2,500 (0.25×) is a TEST value, not a proposal.

fields.name: total_written_off
docs: Venue losses absorbed by the treasury through `write_off_advance`.

fields.name: action
docs: 0 = paired mint; 1 = paired redeem.

fields.name: collateral_amount
docs: Actual collateral paid by / returned to the user.

fields.name: gross_collateral_amount
docs: Mint input / redeem payout before the explicit fee.

types.name: RedemptionAmounts
docs: `request_redemption` arguments, in ONE struct (the v1.45 toolchain
miscompiles per-argument borsh offsets on multi-arg instructions).

types.name: RedemptionRequest
docs: A paired redemption waiting for the keeper to pay it (r58 lever 1 + 2).
PDA seeds: `[b"redemption", market, owner]`, so one open request per
(market, owner). The escrowed L and S sit in two token accounts owned by
this PDA (`[b"redemption_escrow", request, mint]`); their balances always
equal `l_remaining` / `s_remaining`. The tokens stay in supply until a
settle burns them, so a waiting request changes no CR or haircut.
Lives in its own account, never in `Market` (Anchor deserializes before
realloc; see `market_space_tests`).

fields.name: gross_paid
docs: Running totals over all fills (cUSDC atoms).

types.name: RiskFeeConfig
docs: Configuration for risk-based fee adjustments

fields.name: proxy_fee_multiplier
docs: Fee multiplier for Proxy Mode (100 = 1x, 200 = 2x)

fields.name: stress_fee_multiplier
docs: Fee multiplier for Stress mode (100 = 1x, 300 = 3x)
Also the starting point for Recovery Dutch auction (decays to 1.0x over 1 hour)

fields.name: stress_mint_cap
docs: Mint cap per transaction in Stress mode (0 = disabled)

fields.name: allow_mint_in_stress
docs: Whether to allow new mints in Stress mode

fields.name: allow_redeem_in_stress
docs: Whether to allow redeems in Stress mode

types.name: RiskState
docs: Risk state for graduated oracle gating (mirrors oracle program)

types.name: SetGammaParams
docs: Arguments for `set_s_gamma_index`, in ONE struct.
Not two loose arguments: the v1.45 build toolchain miscompiles per-argument
borsh offsets on multi-arg instructions (it once read a fee out of the middle
of a pubkey), and a single struct is the shape that survives it. The wire
format is identical either way, so this costs nothing.

fields.name: s_gamma_index
docs: The new γ index (1e9). Must already be in `[GAMMA_FLOOR, GAMMA_ONE]` —
out-of-range is rejected, never clamped.

fields.name: expected_epoch
docs: The `gamma_epoch` this post was computed against. A compare-and-swap:
the keeper snapshots γ at the start of a cycle and posts later, so
without this a re-anchor landing in that window would let a stale post
re-charge the entire folded epoch, and the ratchet would accept it.

fields.name: max_l_amount
docs: Most L to settle in this call (`u64::MAX` = all that fits). The
program shrinks it to what the vault's cash covers.

types.name: WorstCaseQuotingConfig
docs: Configuration for worst-case quoting
Protects protocol from informed traders exploiting confidence interval edges

fields.name: enabled
docs: Whether worst-case quoting is enabled

fields.name: normal_confidence_multiplier
docs: Confidence multiplier in Normal state (100 = 1x, 150 = 1.5x)

fields.name: proxy_confidence_multiplier
docs: Confidence multiplier in Proxy state

fields.name: stress_confidence_multiplier
docs: Confidence multiplier in Stress state (also the starting point for Recovery Dutch auction)
